name: Avar-Persian siege of Constantinople
summary: In June–August 626, while Emperor Heraclius campaigns in Persia, a combined Avar-Slav-Persian force besieges Constantinople from both the European and Asian sides. The Avars and Slavs attack the Theodosian Walls from the west with siege machinery; Persian forces under Shahrbaraz hold the Asian shore and coordinate by signal fire. The Byzantine navy prevents the Avars from ferrying Persian troops across the Bosphorus; a naval skirmish destroys the Slav boats attempting the crossing. The Avars raise the siege in August 626 after a final assault fails. The 'Akathistos Hymn' is sung in thanksgiving, still sung in Orthodox liturgy annually.

_quarry.structural_significance: The most serious threat to Constantinople before the Arab sieges; the failure of the combined Avar-Persian assault demonstrates the Theodosian Walls' near-impregnability; Heraclius's subsequent campaigns destroy the Sasanian Empire (627–628), only for both powers to fall to the Arab conquests a decade later
